description: baseline

Replace torch.geqrf for n=512 batched cases with a CUTE DSL blocked Householder QR kernel that maps one matrix to a persistent CTA cluster, computes panel norms/reductions and trailing updates in tiled shared memory, and falls back to torch.geqrf for larger n until correctness is proven.
Added a guarded CUTE DSL qr512 probe path, but the n=512 invariance guard failed, so this attempt is invalid.

Added a CUTE DSL n=512 scaffold that compiles and launches only when cutlass.cute is importable, otherwise safely falls back to torch.geqrf. Local environment lacks cutlass.cute, so metric reflects fallback/no-op behavior.

Best valid metric was 115710.042 us at 0510b1f3, only a noise-level improvement over baseline and still torch.geqrf-backed. A direct CUTE n=512 output-touching probe compiled but corrupted Householder factors and failed invariance validation; same-run peer logs show routed CUTE launches also hitting MLIR exceptions. Final profile captured for 0510b1f3. Next brief should either install/diagnose stable CUTLASS DSL multiprocessing launch support first, or switch away from CUTE DSL toward torch/CUDA extension approaches for QR.

Stabilize CUTE DSL availability and multiprocessing launch inside submission.py, then build a correctness-gated n=512 panel diagnostic kernel that computes Householder norms and tau for one panel but falls back to torch.geqrf unless compact H/tau validation passes for every checked matrix.

Added a CUTE DSL n=512 panel diagnostic kernel that computes first-column Householder tau/beta for sampled matrices, caches availability after compact validation, and keeps torch.geqrf as the correctness-gated output path.
Expanded the CUTE panel diagnostic gate to validate tau/beta for every n=512 matrix in the checked batch before enabling the scaffold, still falling back to torch.geqrf for outputs.

Brief exhausted. Stabilized CUTE DSL in submission.py: CUTE imports, compiles, launches under multiprocessing, and a n=512 panel diagnostic computes first-column Householder tau/beta correctly. Best metric this brief was 115767.319 us at ff1e8e9a with sampled validation; safer final full-batch gate is 115801.003 us at 2570b493. Both remain torch.geqrf-backed for outputs, so this is a correctness-gated scaffold rather than a speedup. Next brief can extend the validated panel primitive into compact H/tau writes or blocked trailing updates.

Extend the validated CUTE n=512 first-panel primitive into a correctness-gated output-writing path for only the first Householder column: write H[:,1:,0] and tau[:,0], compare against torch.geqrf on sampled matrices inside the dispatch gate, and keep torch.geqrf fallback unless compact H/tau and downstream QR residual checks pass.

Extended the validated CUTE n=512 panel primitive into a guarded output-writing path: torch.geqrf output is patched for H[:,1:,0] and tau[:,0] by CUTE after compact H/tau and residual checks pass on sampled matrices.

Cached the CUTE first-panel compact/residual gate after its first successful sample check so later n=512 calls launch only the output patch after torch.geqrf; validation passed but benchmark regressed versus the uncached iteration within noise.

Restored the per-call sampled compact H/tau and residual gate for the CUTE first-column output writer after the cached gate regressed; final head remains correctness-gated and output-writing for n=512.

Brief exhausted. Built a CUTE DSL n=512 output-writing first-panel path that patches H[:,1:,0] and tau[:,0] after validating compact H/tau and downstream QR residuals against torch.geqrf on sampled matrices, with torch.geqrf fallback on any gate failure. Best metric was 115727.181 us at 185dc36f; final profiled head is 3195418b at 115735.470 us after restoring the safer per-call gate because the cached gate regressed to 115746.560 us. This line proves correctness-gated CUTE output writes but still pays torch.geqrf plus gate/launch overhead, so next work should either replace more of the first panel/trailing update to amortize the CUTE launch or remove redundant torch.geqrf work only after full compact-factor validation is proven.

Extend the valid n=512 CUTE output-writing first-column path to a two-column mini-panel: compute and write Householder columns 0 and 1 plus tau[0:2], apply the first reflector update before the second, and keep fallback unless compact H/tau comparison and downstream QR residual and orthogonality checks pass.

Extended the guarded CUTE QR512 output writer from column 0 to a two-column mini-panel with tau[0:2], first-reflector update before column 1, compact H/tau comparison, QR residual, and orthogonality guard. It validates but local timing is slower than parent.

Renamed the CUTE writer to panel01 and added an independent torch reference for Householder columns 0 and 1 so the CUTE path must match compact H/tau, residual, and orthogonality before replacing torch.geqrf output. Local timing remains fallback/no-op dominated because cutlass.cute is not installed.

Cached the CUTE QR512 two-column panel self-test after the first successful compact/residual/orthogonality guard, so a real CUTE deployment only pays the expensive comparison once per process while retaining fallback safety. Local metric is near fallback because cutlass.cute is absent.

Brief 3 exhausted. Implemented a CUTE QR512 two-column mini-panel writer for Householder columns 0 and 1 with tau[0:2], applying reflector 0 before column 1, plus compact H/tau comparison, independent torch reference, QR residual, orthogonality guard, and cached self-test. All iterations validated; best metric in this brief was f0ca2caf at 115774.435 us, still slightly slower than parent 115727.181 us and baseline/no-op behavior because this host has no cutlass.cute installed, so benchmarks are fallback-dominated. Profiles were captured for iteration 0 and final iteration 2; next useful brief should either run in an environment with cutlass.cute to compile/profile the real kernel or continue extending the guarded panel to more columns only after validating CUTE availability.

Build an exact-shape n=1024 batch-60 structural fast path for near-rank or mixed matrices using cheap per-matrix detection and a CUTE DSL prefix-factor/tau-padding strategy analogous to the valid n=512 rankdef and clustered paths; preserve all existing dispatch arms and fallback unless full validation guards pass.

Added a guarded n=1024 batch-60 structured path: cheap per-matrix rankdef/nearrank/cluster detection routes structured matrices through a 768-column torch.geqrf prefix, torch.ormqr trailing update, and CUTE DSL tau-padding/lower-tail cleanup while preserving dense fallback and existing dispatch arms. Full validation and guards passed; benchmark geomean improved.

Split the n=1024 structured path into exact rankdef/cluster zero-tail and near-rank trailing-update arms so exact structures skip torch.ormqr while near-rank keeps the prefix update. Validation and guards passed; benchmark geomean improved slightly over the unified structured path.

Brief 4 exhausted. Best valid metric is 83696.095 us at 6cb233a7, improving the parent 35637aed and baseline by adding an n=1024 batch-60 structured dispatch. The final path cheaply detects rankdef/nearrank/clustered matrices per batch, sends exact rankdef/cluster matrices through a 768-column prefix QR with CUTE tau padding and zero-tail output, sends near-rank matrices through prefix QR plus ormqr trailing update and CUTE cleanup, and preserves dense fallback plus all existing n=32/176/512/4096 arms. A unified near/rank/cluster path also validated at 83748.447 us, but splitting exact zero-tail from near-rank was slightly faster. Profiles were saved for both iterations; next brief could target reducing detection/indexing overhead for mixed n=1024 or replacing the torch.geqrf prefix with a true CUTE blocked prefix kernel.

Combine the latest QR352 CUTE specialization from 538560b with the n=1024 structural split path from 6cb233a and the n=512 routing-reduction reuse from f699dd5; preserve each exact shape and content dispatch gate, transplant all required helper functions, keep existing QR32, n=176, n=512 structural, and 4096 upper paths, and fall back to torch.geqrf otherwise.

Combined latest 128-thread QR352 CUTE specialization with the split n=1024 structural prefix path and n=512 routing-reduction reuse, preserving exact shape/content gates plus QR32, n176, n512 structural, and 4096 upper fallbacks.

Completed the n=1024 split-path transplant by separating exact rankdef/clustered zero-tail routing from near-rank prefix-plus-ormqr routing while keeping the combined QR352 and n512 route-reuse stack.

Brief 5 exhausted. Best valid head is 863eaae at linalg/qr_v2=81867.224 us, improving the QR352 parent 538560b, n1024 split parent 6cb233a, and n512 routing-reuse parent f699dd5 by stacking all requested exact gates. Iteration 0 combined the 128-thread QR352 CUTE specialization, n1024 structural prefix path, n512 route-reduction reuse, QR32, n176, n512 structural, and 4096 upper paths at 81957.207 us; iteration 1 completed the 6cb233a split by routing exact rankdef/clustered n1024 cases to zero-tail prefix QR and near-rank cases to prefix-plus-ormqr, improving to 81867.224 us. Build, full validation, differential guard, invariance guard, benchmark, and final nsys profiles passed for both commits; profiles are saved for 62f1ee58 and 863eaae5. Remaining bottleneck is still torch.geqrf/dense fallback and routing/reduction overhead, so next useful brief should reduce n1024/n512 mixed indexing overhead or replace torch.geqrf prefix work with a true blocked CUTE implementation.

Reduce combined branch routing and indexing overhead for n=512 and n=1024 mixed structural paths: reuse batch-level reductions across gates, avoid repeated boolean indexing or nonzero calls, and short-circuit dense all-fallback cases before constructing masks, preserving exact predicates and math; keep only if validation passes and geomean improves.

Replaced repeated boolean mixed n512/n1024 indexing with one set of route indices plus index_select/index_copy routing. Full validation and guards passed, but benchmark regressed slightly versus parent.

Merged the n=1024 rankdef/nearrank/cluster predicate setup to share one abs(data) tensor and head/tail reductions while preserving exact routing and CUTE tau/cleanup paths. Full validation, guards, and benchmark passed with a small geomean improvement.
Also reused one n=512 abs tail slice to derive tail384 and tail260 reductions. Full validation and guards passed, but benchmark regressed versus the n1024-only predicate-sharing commit.

Brief 6 exhausted. Best valid head is dbc322f4 at linalg/qr_v2=81859.809 us, improving parent 863eaae5 by merging n=1024 structural predicate setup to share a single abs(data) tensor and reused head/tail reductions while preserving the exact rankdef/cluster/near gates and existing CUTE tau/cleanup paths. An index_select/index_copy routing rewrite validated but regressed to 81891.954 us, and an additional n=512 shared-tail reduction attempt validated but regressed to 81880.924 us, so the branch is reset to dbc322f4. Build, full validation, differential guard, invariance guard, benchmark, and final nsys profile passed for the best commit; profile saved under profiles/2026-06-24-09-37-42-qrv2_kernel_languages_pcevwrpue for dbc322f4. Next useful brief could replace the remaining PyTorch predicate reductions/nonzero-style mask handling with a tiny CUTE/CUDA classification kernel for n=512/n=1024 or attack torch.geqrf prefix work directly.

Replace the QR352 implementation in the stacked dbc322f4 branch with the 16-column batched QR352 CUTE update path from 31f5bdca; preserve all n=1024 predicate-sharing helpers, n=512 routing-reduction paths, QR32, n=176, n=512 structural, 4096 upper paths, exact dispatch gates, and torch.geqrf fallback.

Combined the stacked dbc322f4 dispatch/helpers with the 31f5bdca sixteen-column QR352 CUTE update path, preserving QR32, QR176, 4096 upper identity, n=1024 predicate sharing, n=512 routing reductions, and geqrf fallback.
Amended the combine to restore the exact dbc322f4 n=1024 near-rank predicate while keeping the 31f5bdca sixteen-column QR352 CUTE update path and all stacked dispatch routes.

Brief 7 exhausted. Best valid head is 3b663021 at linalg/qr_v2=75864.246 us: it combines the 31f5bdca 16-column batched QR352 CUTE update path with the stacked dbc322f4 routes/helpers, and restores the exact dbc322f4 n=1024 near-rank predicate after an initial combine drift. Build, full validation, differential guard, invariance guard, benchmark, and final nsys profile passed; profile saved as worker-0-brief-7-iteration-1-3b6630217bd735fae34d089751168d21363da86e.nsys-rep. Next useful brief: attack remaining PyTorch predicate/mask reductions with a small CUTE classification kernel, or replace prefix geqrf/ormqr structural paths.

Replace only the QR352 batching implementation in the combined best 3b663021 branch with the 24-column QR352 CUTE update kernel from 92a1e12; preserve all stacked n=1024 predicate-sharing helpers, n=512 routing-reduction paths, QR32, n=176, n=512 structural, 4096 upper paths, exact gates, and torch.geqrf fallback.
Transplanted the donor 24-column QR352 CUTE update kernel onto the combined best branch; validation passed, but the full benchmark exceeded the 120s budget before reporting a metric.
